sections.title: Vertical Integration: From Power to Compute
sections.body: Kenya AI Compute is not a traditional cloud provider; it is an infrastructure asset that controls its own supply chain. By integrating the data center directly with a 2MW+ hybrid power plant, we eliminate the volatility of the public grid and secure the lowest energy rates available for high-performance computing. Our facility utilizes a modular, containerized approach that allows for rapid deployment and easy maintenance. The compute architecture is a balanced hybrid: 30% dedicated to high-end GPU clusters for AI training and rendering, 50% dedicated to CPU workloads for inference and general-purpose edge computing, and 20% dedicated to high-speed NVMe storage. This mix is specifically engineered to ensure high utilization rates across both enterprise clients and decentralized DePIN protocols. Additional context: the project follows a clear rollout roadmap that aligns low-cost energy, infrastructure reliability, and flexible deployment models. sections.title: Project Fundamentals
items: Facility Type: Modular containerized data center with advanced environmental controls.
Energy Supply: Direct captive generation (Solar + Gas/Diesel backup) at $0.04/kWh.
Compute Profile: Hybrid 30/50/20 (GPU/CPU/Storage) for diverse revenue streams.
Reliability: Designed to Tier II/III standards with 99.9% guaranteed uptime.
Profitability: Target EBITDA of 35-50% with a 5-7 year payback period.
